parsed.explanation: Combined regime has federal border/document/facility exposures that a protective state cannot cancel. Trans visa/passport mismatch can trigger refusal, evidence demands, and permanent fraud ineligibility; reported passport blocks/stranding. Federal corrections/immigration custody documents abuse, conversion-therapy-style treatment, beatings, solitary, sexual harm. Many state facility bans and a capitol arrest increase facility risk, though this state’s public-accommodation, hate-crime, panic-defense repeal, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms, and healthcare shield laws reduce local service risk for adults and care-seeking travellers. Enforcement of shield/public accommodation is not documented, and federal facilities remain hostile. A traveller with a minor faces school/social-transition prosecution and document scrutiny. Severe but not imprisonment/execution likely; high risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal sex-based passport/visa rules, X ban; discrepancy or reasonable doubt sex triggers refusal/additional evidence; suspected misrepresentation can support permanent ineligibility; reports of blocks/stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Protective state public-accommodation and marriage laws; foreign advisories caution travellers; no border shield documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening can become immigration/fraud investigation before state local protections matter.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, sexual abuse; federal corrections adopts conversion-therapy-style rules and hormone removal.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Litigation against passport rules and hate-crime statute exist; not shown to prevent federal custody placement or abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch or suspected fraud can move a traveller into federal custody; state shield cannot block detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; many state/provinces ban identity-congruent facilities; capitol restroom arrest shows criminalization.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State nondiscrimination covers public accommodations/education; single-user bathrooms neutral; no documented local multi-user ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State nondiscrimination does not preempt federal or federally funded facilities and border-adjacent spaces.

care_services.exposure: National minor-care hostility, school/social-transition prosecution, funding blocks; federal emergency/facility placement uncertain.
care_services.protection: State shield laws protect travel for gender-affirming care; insurer coverage mandates and public-accommodation law exist.
care_services.interaction: Shield may protect care within state, but entry screening or federal custody can make care-seeking an investigation.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders/counterterrorism language frame radical transgender ideology as violent-extremist context; public support birth-sex documents; allied advisories follow detentions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State nondiscrimination and hate-crime law remain on books; national employment ruling exists but is under federal attack.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing may embolden federal screeners and facility staff; local officers may apply state protections.

minors_guardians.exposure: Passport mismatch scrutiny, school/social-transition criminalization, minor care bans elsewhere; guardians may face fraud questions for inconsistent child documents.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield for travel-for-care, student protections, anti-bullying policy, conversion-therapy ban, local sports/education rules.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family school/sport/health encounters can disclose status; local law mitigates, federal orders threaten investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific visitor violence campaign; misgendering or service friction possible, especially at federal spaces.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State public-accommodation law bars service discrimination; hate-crime enhancements and panic-defense repeal are documented on books.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police complaint response not documented; federal security personnel may still detain, exclude, or verify documents.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Border refusal/fraud bar, immigration detention abuse, facility arrest possible; no documented operative federal preemption relief.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, legal-aid FAQ, state shield and nondiscrimination statutes.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Pending litigation may slow but not reliably reverse operative screening/custody rules; state enforcement unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A’s border exclusion without arrest is comparable, but this combined regime adds credible immigration/custody abuse, fraud bars, and federal facility bans. Protective-state local service law offsets some risk, leaving it slightly lower than the border-exclusion anchor.

0.55-B has extended screening and administrative refusal without criminal prosecution. Here the federal layer is harsher—possible permanent fraud ineligibility and severe immigration custody—while state nondiscrimination and shield laws make local stay safer. Net result is below 0.55-B but not in the 0.35-only border-denial band.

0.75-C assumes identity-respecting entry and functioning tribunals. This regime fails that: passports/visas enforce birth-sex and can deny entry; federal custody/facilities are hostile. State protections are real but do not cover federal screening/custody, so the rating is materially lower than 0.75-C.

0.25-C has frequent raids and birth-sex prison placement. Here no documented visitor raids occur, and protective-state public-accommodation law reduces local exposure; federal border/custody hostility keeps it near 0.25-C rather than elevated.

parsed.synthesis: Federal entry screening dominates. A mismatch or sex doubt can produce refusal, further investigation, and possible permanent fraud bar; if custody follows, federal immigration and corrections settings have documented abuse and identity erasure. Protective state law improves hotels, restaurants, healthcare travel, and some facilities, but does not preempt federal borders, federally funded spaces, or federal detention. For adults, harm concentrates at federal touchpoints and facility checks; for minors, school/social-transition criminalization and guardian document scrutiny add exposure. Remedies are pending and local enforcement is not documented, so protections are meaningful but not reliable. The result is high risk, not catastrophic.
